use classicmodels;
show tables;

#Assignment 5

#Q-1
select Sum(amount) from payments;

#Q-2
select * from customers;
select count(*),max(creditLimit),min(creditLimit),avg(creditLimit)from customers;

#Q-3
select max(buyPrice),min(buyPrice),avg(buyPrice)from products;


#Q-4
select country,count(*) from customers group by country;

#Q-5
select * from employees;
select officeCode,count(*) from employees group by officeCode;

#Q-6
select * from products;
select productLine,count(*) from products group by productLine;

#Q-7
select * from customers order by creditLimit desc;

#Q-8
select * from products order by buyPrice asc;

#Q-9
select * from employees;
alter table  employees add column fullname varchar(255);
update employees set fullname=concat(firstName,' ',lastName);

select * from employees order by fullname asc;

#Q-10
select customerName,creditLimit from customers order by creditLimit desc limit 5;

#Q-11
select productName,buyPrice from products order by buyPrice limit 10;

#Q-12
select orderNumber,orderDate from orders order by orderDate desc limit 7;

#Q-13
select country from customers group by country having count(customerName)>5;

#Q-14
select * from products;
select productLine from products group by productLine having count(*)>10;

#Q-15
select officeCode from employees group by officeCode having count(*)>2;

#Q-16
select c.customerName,o.orderNumber,o.orderDate from customers as c inner join orders as o on c.customerNumber=o.customerNumber;

#Q-17
select e.fullname,o.city,o.country from employees as e inner join offices as o on e.officeCode = o.officeCode;

#Q-18
select c.customerName,o.orderNumber from customers as c left join orders as o on (c.customerNumber=o.customerNumber or c.customerNumber=NULL);

#Q-19
select e.fullname,c.customerName from employees as e left join customers as c on c.salesRepEmployeeNumber=e.employeeNumber;

#Q-20
#Full join is not supported directly in MYSQL so do(left-join,union,right-join)
(select c.customerName,o.orderNumber from customers as c left join orders as o on o.customerNumber=c.customerNumber) union (select c.customerName,o.orderNumber from customers as c right join orders as o on o.customerNumber=c.customerNumber);


#get the second highest profit of the product
select max(profit) from products where profit<(select max(profit) from products);


create database college;
use college;




#student table
create table students(
	id int primary key auto_increment,
    student_name varchar(255) not null,
    branch varchar(255)
);
alter table students add column admission_year int;
alter table students rename column branch to branch_id,rename column id to student_id;



#faculty table
create table faculty(
	id int primary key auto_increment,
    faculty_name varchar(255) not null,
    branch varchar(255),
    post varchar(255) not null
);
alter table faculty rename column teacher_id to faculty_id ;
alter table faculty rename column branch to branch_id ;
alter table faculty modify column post int ;
alter table faculty rename column post to experience;





create table branch(
	branch_id int primary key auto_increment,
    branch_name varchar(255),
    hod_name varchar(255),
    office_number int
);




create table courses(
	course_id int primary key auto_increment,
    course_name varchar(255),
    branch_id int,
    faculty_id int
);

#continue with primary key
